entity-newcomer-after-settlescene-entity-transitions0.75 of 0.75 (major)passRequirement met. Newcomers become visible only after a 0.65s delay that applies to their entry alone. The continuing entities&#39; layout motion is never given a duration or a delay. (1) Newcomer path: Appear (Appear.tsx:4-5) starts at opacity 0 and animates opacity to 1 with {duration: ENTER_T, delay}. The delay defaults to ENTER_DELAY = 0.65 (constants.ts:4). In the sample, New (sample-scene.tsx:27-29) wraps its children in Appear. That covers every entity introduced after step 1: conversation-link, skill and question-chip (34-38), step-card-N (43), verify (51), depth-control (55), scene-kit (57-60), modify and edited-card (61-64), and outer-frame (65). ghost-card is wrapped directly in Appear inside AnimatePresence (52-53). (2) Continuing path: every kit primitive the sample uses renders `motion.div layout layoutId={id}` with no transition and no delay (Box.tsx:16, Label.tsx:4, Arrow.tsx:4, SymbolChip.tsx:4, Emphasis.tsx:4, Frame.tsx:4). No primitive reads ENTER_DELAY, so the delay is not added to continuing layout motion. Nothing in the render chain supplies a layout transition either: Talk.tsx:5, then Presentation.tsx:20-27, then Stage.tsx:12-19, which renders only a LayoutGroup, an AnimatePresence and a wrapper motion.div. No MotionConfig appears anywhere. LAYOUT_T = 0.65 (constants.ts:2) is applied only to the scene wrapper&#39;s opacity (Stage.tsx:15). Because all steps share groupKey &#39;reference-sample&#39; (sample-scene.tsx:81), that wrapper keeps its key and does not replay between steps. Persisting entities therefore use motion&#39;s built-in default layout transition (0.45s). Even taking LAYOUT_T = 0.65 as the upper bound, ENTER_DELAY = 0.65 is at least as long, so a newcomer&#39;s visible entry starts after the continuing layout transition ends. engineering-preview-readiness-boundedengineering-verification-tooling-robustness0 of 0.625 (major)failI rule judge B&#39;s and judge C&#39;s fail. The timeout clause is met: there is a 30 s timer in startPreview. The build-first clause is also met: both scripts await `npm run build` before startPreview. The parsing clause is not met. Readiness depends on the server&#39;s printed `Local:` URL, and the review guidance names output split across chunks as a failure case. In both copies of preview-process.mjs, the ANSI strip `chunk.replace(/\u001b\[[0-9;]*m/g, &#39;&#39;)` runs on each chunk before it is appended. If a colour escape is split between two chunks, neither half matches, and the stray bytes stay in `output`. The URL regex `/Local:\s+(http:\/\/127\.0\.0\.1:\d+\/?)/` also has no terminator after the port digits. A chunk that ends mid-port, such as `...127.0.0.1:41` followed by `73/`, matches at once and resolves `settled` with a truncated, wrong URL. The readiness parsing therefore does not tolerate output split across chunks. Judge A&#39;s pass rests on the claim that matching accumulated output handles split chunks. Fixed: review_._all-reviewers (1) - src/presentation-kit/useFitScale.ts:12 Precondition: the stage is rendered. `useFitScale` measures the Stage `<section>`, which is a `flex: 1` child. The header, TOC and footer are already outside it. Execution trace: `calculateFitScale` then subtracts `STAGE_LAYOUT[mode].top` and `.bottom` (112 and 172 in browse mode, 84 and 72 in present mode) from that already-reduced height. Failure: the canvas is scaled down for the chrome twice. It renders much smaller than the space available, and it is clamped to MIN_SCALE on short viewports such as landscape phones. The unit test uses synthetic numbers, so it does not catch this. Fix: either measure the full root and keep the chrome offsets, or measure the stage and subtract only the horizontal padding and a small margin, e.g. `const availableHeight = Math.max(0, height - geometry.vertical)`.\n ✓ Fixed: review_._all-reviewers (1) - src/main.tsx:8 Precondition: a presentation chunk fails to load, for example because of a network error or a stale deploy hash. Execution trace: `lazy(entry.load)` rejects. `App` only wraps `Route` in `Suspense` and has no error boundary. Failure: React 19 unmounts the whole root and shows a blank page, with no message and no link back to the landing page. Fix: wrap `<Route />` in an error boundary that renders a fallback message and a link to `/`.\n ✓ Fixed: review_._all-reviewers (1) - src/presentation-kit/Presentation.tsx:11 Precondition: the `steps` prop gets shorter while the current index is at or past the new length, for example after hot reload or when the caller filters steps. Execution trace: `nav.index` is stored in state and only clamped when `goTo`, `next` or `prev` is called. `steps[nav.index]` is then `undefined`. Failure: `Header` reads `step.era` and `Footer` reads `step.caption`, so the component throws a TypeError. Buttons and links now navigate with Arrow and Page keys, and Space is only swallowed on them for native activation. Ancestor `role` and `tabindex` wrappers no longer block navigation. The fix does add a regression. `ARROW_WIDGET` is tested with `target.matches(...)` on the focused element only, but the container roles in it (`tablist`, `listbox`, `menu`, `tree`, `grid`) normally don't hold focus. Focus sits on their children: `[role=tab]`, `[role=option]`, `[role=menuitem]`, `[role=treeitem]`, `[role=gridcell]`. Trace: an author's presentation has a `role=tablist` with roving tabindex, and the user focuses a `role=tab` and presses ArrowRight. `target.matches(ARROW_WIDGET)` is false because the target is the tab, not the tablist. The guard doesn't fire, so `preventDefault()` and `next()` run. Failure: arrow keys advance the slide instead of moving between tabs, options, or menu items, and the widget's own keydown handling is pre-empted. Both points are accurate. Talk.tsx passes `title`, and Header.tsx renders it as the browse-mode h1. But the dissent never answers the majority&#39;s reason for failing: the demo carries a dead and misleading contract. The review guidance says to score that kind of contract under this criterion. The source shows that contract: - **Unused payload field:** `SamplePayload` in sample-scene.tsx declares `entities: string[]`, and all nine `scenes` entries fill it in. `STEPS` passes each entry as the step&#39;s payload, and Stage.tsx hands `step.payload` to the Scene. `SampleScene` reads `showSkill`, `showQuestion`, `cards`, `showModify`, `showVerify`, `showDepth`, `showKit` and `reveal`, but never `payload.entities`. Presentation passes the current step to Stage, which renders step.Scene inside LayoutGroup and AnimatePresence. SampleScene is typed as the kit&#39;s Scene&lt;SamplePayload&gt; and builds its entities from the kit nodes Label, Box, Arrow, SymbolChip, Emphasis and Frame. Each node forwards its id to motion.div layoutId. STEPS is Step&lt;SamplePayload&gt;[] and supplies the kit&#39;s fields. Navigation and morphing are not reimplemented in the demo. All nine steps come from one map in sample-scene.tsx, so that module covers them.","evidence":["Talk.tsx: &lt;Presentation steps={STEPS} title=... initialMode=&quot;browse&quot; /&gt;","sample-scene.tsx imports the kit nodes and the Scene and Step types, and defines STEPS through one titles.map","Box.tsx and the other node files: motion.div layout layoutId={id}","Stage.tsx: LayoutGroup, AnimatePresence, &lt;Scene payload={step.payload} .../&gt;"],"citations":["src/presentations/how-to-make-a-presentation/Talk.tsx","src/presentations/how-to-make-a-presentation/steps/sample-scene.tsx","src/presentation-kit/Presentation.tsx","src/presentation-kit/Stage.tsx","src/presentation-kit/types.ts","src/presentation-kit/nodes/Box.tsx","src/presentation-kit/nodes/Arrow.tsx"],"marker":""},{"id":"demo-stable-identity-and-grouping","classification":"confirmed","rationale":"Grouping: the single map in sample-scene.tsx gives all nine steps Scene: SampleScene and groupKey &#39;reference-sample&#39;. Stage derives identity as group:&lt;groupKey&gt; and uses it as the motion.div key, so the key is constant across steps and the Scene instance updates in place. The third clause is not met. Readiness depends on the printed Local URL, and the ANSI strip runs on each chunk before the text is accumulated. Output split across chunks is therefore only tolerated when the split falls outside an escape sequence. If a colour escape such as `\\x1b[36m` is split across two chunks, the per-chunk regex strips neither half. The accumulated text then keeps the stray escape bytes between `Local:` and `http://`, and the match fails until the 30s timeout. The correct design is to accumulate raw output and strip after. The integration test points the reference at an unregistered slug and asserts a non-zero exit and output containing &#39;sample&#39;. Judge B argues that an empty steps array only produces a render-hook timeout. That is a corner case the guidance does not require separately. preview` directly with process.execPath, so `started.child` is the preview server itself and not an npm or npx wrapper. In both scripts, `preview = started.child` is assigned straight after startPreview, before any await. The readiness wait, chromium.launch, and every page operation all sit inside the `try`, so success, a failing check, a browser launch failure, and any error after the preview started all pass through `finally { await cleanup() }`. cleanup() closes the browser, sends SIGTERM to the preview child, and awaits its &#39;exit&#39; event. The template copies have the same code, and presentation-template.test.ts asserts byte parity with the repository scripts. Judge C&#39;s reason is that cleanup does not await another exit event after the SIGKILL escalation. That does not decide the requirement. SIGKILL only runs as a fallback if the server ignores SIGTERM for 3 s, and it cannot be caught, so the server is still terminated. On every named exit path, the primary mechanism is to terminate the server itself and await its exit, and the source has that on all four paths. Readiness depends on the server&#39;s printed `Local:` URL, and the review guidance names output split across chunks as a failure case. In both copies of preview-process.mjs, the ANSI strip `chunk.replace(/\\u001b\\[[0-9;]*m/g, &#39;&#39;)` runs on each chunk before it is appended. If a colour escape is split between two chunks, neither half matches, and the stray bytes stay in `output`. The URL regex `/Local:\\s+(http:\\/\\/127\\.0\\.0\\.1:\\d+\\/?)/` also has no terminator after the port digits. A chunk that ends mid-port, such as `...127.0.0.1:41` followed by `73/`, matches at once and resolves `settled` with a truncated, wrong URL. The readiness parsing therefore does not tolerate output split across chunks. Judge A&#39;s pass rests on the claim that matching accumulated output handles split chunks. In both scripts, `preview = started.child` is assigned straight after startPreview, before any await. The readiness wait, chromium.launch, and every page operation all sit inside the `try`, so success, a failing check, a browser launch failure, and any error after the preview started all pass through `finally { await cleanup() }`. cleanup() closes the browser, sends SIGTERM to the preview child, and awaits its &#39;exit&#39; event. The template copies have the same code, and presentation-template.test.ts asserts byte parity with the repository scripts. Judge C&#39;s reason is that cleanup does not await another exit event after the SIGKILL escalation. That does not decide the requirement. SIGKILL only runs as a fallback if the server ignores SIGTERM for 3 s, and it cannot be caught, so the server is still terminated. On every named exit path, the primary mechanism is to terminate the server itself and await its exit, and the source has that on all four paths. The criterion targets wrapper-only kills and paths that skip cleanup, and neither occurs here.","evidence":["scripts/preview-process.mjs:5 spawnProcess(process.execPath, [vite, &#39;preview&#39;, &#39;--host&#39;, &#39;127.0.0.1&#39;, &#39;--port&#39;, &#39;0&#39;]) — the child is the Vite server process it…","scripts/verify.mjs:25-32 cleanup(): browser.close, then preview.kill(&#39;SIGTERM&#39;), then await Promise.race([preview.once(&#39;exit&#39;), delay(3000)]), then SIGKILL as a fallback.","scripts/verify.mjs:56-59 preview = started.child is assigned before awaiting ready, and chromium.launch is inside the try; The timeout clause is met: there is a 30 s timer in startPreview. The build-first clause is also met: both scripts await `npm run build` before startPreview. The parsing clause is not met. Readiness depends on the server&#39;s printed `Local:` URL, and the review guidance names output split across chunks as a failure case. In both copies of preview-process.mjs, the ANSI strip `chunk.replace(/\\u001b\\[[0-9;]*m/g, &#39;&#39;)` runs on each chunk before it is appended. If a colour escape is split between two chunks, neither half matches, and the stray bytes stay in `output`. The URL regex `/Local:\\s+(http:\\/\\/127\\.0\\.0\\.1:\\d+\\/?)/` also has no terminator after the port digits. A chunk that ends mid-port, such as `...127.0.0.1:41` followed by `73/`, matches at once and resolves `settled` with a truncated, wrong URL. The readiness parsing therefore does not tolerate output split across chunks. Judge A&#39;s pass rests on the claim that matching accumulated output handles split chunks. The source contradicts that claim in both cases above. preview-process.test.ts writes each Local line as one clean, uncoloured chunk, so no test covers either case.","evidence":["scripts/preview-process.mjs:25 output += chunk.replace(/\\u001b\\[[0-9;]*m/g, &#39;&#39;) strips ANSI codes per chunk, so an escape split across chunks survives in the accumulated output.","scripts/preview-process.mjs:26-29 match /Local:\\s+(http:\\/\\/127\\.0\\.0\\.1:\\d+\\/?)/ has no end anchor after the digits, so a chunk ending mid-port resolves readiness at once with a truncated port.","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/preview-process.mjs:25-29 has the same code; both verify and inspect copies depend on it.","src/scripts/preview-process.test.ts:36 writes the full uncoloured line &#39; Local: http://127.0.0.1:43127/\\n&#39; in one chunk; there is no split or ANSI case.","The other two clauses hold (preview-process.mjs:34 has the 30 s timeout; verify.mjs:41 and inspect-presentation.mjs:36-40 await the build), but the criterion fails when any one clause is unmet."],"citations":[{"path":"scripts/preview-process.mjs","start_line":22,"end_line":36},{"path":"skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/preview-process.mjs","start_line":22,"end_line":36},{"path":"src/scripts/preview-process.test.ts","start_line":30,"end_line":38}],"search_scope":[],"missing_obligation":""},{"id":"engineering-tests-wait-on-state","verdict":"pass","rationale":"The tests that drive a browser are the two integration suites, tests/integration/scripts.test.ts and tests/integration/presentation-template.test.ts. Neither has a sleep: the only setTimeout in either, at scripts.test.ts:25 and presentation-template.test.ts:20, is a kill-on-timeout guard. Each test awaits the child&#39;s &#39;exit&#39; event and then asserts on the exit code and output. The only other bounded wait is the socket timeout at scripts.test.ts:170, a connect probe that settles when the probe resolves. In the browser scripts, every step assertion is preceded by an auto-waiting or polling wait on state. verify.mjs waits for the presentation root locator at line 71 (timeout 10000) and again for visibility at line 77. It waits for the mode attribute with waitForFunction at lines 84 and 90, for the title and caption locators to be visible at lines 86 and 92, and for data-step-index to equal the next step with waitForFunction at line 100. So the getAttribute read at line 78 always follows a state wait: line 71 for the first step, and line 100 from the previous iteration for later steps. It is not an immediate read used as a wait. inspect-presentation.mjs likewise waits for the root at line 49 and polls data-step-index with waitForFunction at line 57 before each later step. The jsdom component tests also use polling waitFor on data-step-index (Presentation.test.tsx:42-46, how-to-make-a-presentation.test.tsx:45). Judges A and B voted pass, and that is the ruling. Judge C points to inspect&#39;s `await page.waitForTimeout(settle)` (inspect-presentation.mjs:59) and the test&#39;s elapsed-time check `toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(300)` (scripts.test.ts:140). That fact does not decide the requirement. The criterion fails a test only when it sleeps a fixed time instead of waiting for state before asserting the step. Here the settle delay runs only after the state wait for the step index at line 57 has already confirmed the step. It is an extra animation settle before the screenshot, not a stand-in for the step wait. The elapsed-time assertion only checks that the --settle option is honoured. It is a time check, not a sleep in the test. Tests that start a preview or a browser do so through verify and inspect, which call startPreview. startPreview launches Vite with `--port 0`, so the OS assigns the port, and the unit test asserts those arguments. Readiness reads the port Vite announces, and no test or script hardcodes a port. Each integration file works in its own mkdtemp copy. The tests never kill a wrapper as their normal teardown. The scripts exit on their own after their finally cleanup has sent SIGTERM to the Vite server itself, awaited its exit, and closed Chromium. scripts.test.ts confirms the listener is gone after the failure runs with an ECONNREFUSED probe. Judge C&#39;s reason is that the SIGKILL on the test&#39;s timeout path bypasses the scripts&#39; cleanup. That path only runs if a script hangs past 180–300 s, and the runs the tests produce do not reach it, because every script wait is bounded. The criterion&#39;s defect is a test whose termination kills only a wrapper and leaves the server running. The child is therefore the preview server itself, not an npm or npx wrapper. In the template verify script (lines 40-60), the top-level `try` opens at line 40. `preview = started.child` is assigned at line 57, before the readiness await and before chromium.launch. The matching top-level catch/finally at lines 106-111 calls `await cleanup()`. The repository and template inspect scripts have the same layout: try at 35, preview assigned at 43, launch at 45, finally cleanup at 98-99. The repository verify script&#39;s quoted lines 25-35, 54-60 and 106-111 match the template&#39;s line for line, and the parity test asserts the repository and template scripts are byte-identical. cleanup closes the browser, sends SIGTERM to the server child, awaits its &#39;exit&#39; event (bounded at 3 s) and escalates to SIGKILL, which cannot be caught. A success, a failing check, a browser launch failure and an error after the preview started therefore all terminate the server process itself.","evidence":["scripts/preview-process.mjs:5 spawns process.execPath with [vite, &#39;preview&#39;, ...]: the server itself, not a wrapper.","scripts/verify.mjs:25-32 / scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs:23-30: cleanup sends SIGTERM to preview, awaits &#39;exit&#39; (raced with 3 s), then SIGKILL.","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/verify.mjs:40-60: try opens at 40; preview = started.child at 57 precedes await ready (58) and chromium.launch (59).","scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs:35-45 and the template copy: try at 35, preview assigned at 43 before ready and launch.","verify.mjs:106-111 and inspect-presentation.mjs:95-100 (both copies): finally { await cleanup() }.","tests/integration/presentation-template.test.ts:43-45 asserts byte parity of verify/inspect/preview-process between the bootstrap template and the repository."],"citations":["scripts/preview-process.mjs","scripts/verify.mjs","scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/verify.mjs","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/preview-process.mjs","tests/integration/presentation-template.test.ts"],"marker":"","scope_repair":[],"criterion":"engineering-preview-terminated-on-every-exit","cycle":"initial","part":0},{"id":"engineering-preview-readiness-bounded","classification":"confirmed","rationale":"Readiness depends on the server&#39;s printed `Local:` URL, so the parsing clause applies. The review guidance names output split across chunks as a failure case. In both copies of preview-process.mjs, the ANSI strip runs on each incoming chunk before it is appended (line 25). A colour escape split across two chunks is therefore never removed from the accumulated output. The URL regex `/Local:\\s+(http:\\/\\/127\\.0\\.0\\.1:\\d+\\/?)/` is tested after every chunk and has no terminator after the port digits. A chunk boundary inside the port number makes the regex match at once, and `settled` resolves with a truncated port. The parsing clause is unmet, which fails the requirement. However, the requirement also needs every started process terminated. The guidance names a test that kills only an npm wrapper and leaves the preview running as a failure. presentation-template.test.ts runs verify and inspect through `npm ... run verify/inspect` (lines 83, 86). Its termination path (line 20) sends `child.kill(&#39;SIGKILL&#39;)` to that npm process only. SIGKILL cannot be caught or forwarded. The verify/inspect node process and the Vite preview it spawned receive no signal, and the scripts&#39; cleanup runs only on their own completion or on SIGINT/SIGTERM. So when this path fires, the preview is left running. The claim argues this path is never reached because every script wait is bounded. The quoted scripts contradict that: `npm run build` runs before the preview with no timeout. The test&#39;s termination code is the wrapper-only kill the guidance names.","evidence":["tests/integration/presentation-template.test.ts:16,20: `spawn(command, args...)` with command = npm, and the timeout handler `child.kill(&#39;SIGKILL&#39;)` targets only that process.","tests/integration/presentation-template.test.ts:83,86: verify and inspect are launched through `npm --prefix ... run`.","scripts/verify.mjs:33-35 / scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs:31-33: script cleanup is reached only via SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers or finally, not on a SIGKILL of the parent npm.","scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs:36-40: npm run build is awaited with no timeout, so the claim that the timeout path is unreachable is unsupported.","scripts/preview-process.mjs:5: `--port 0` meets the dynamic-port clause, but that alone does not satisfy the termination clause."],"citations":["tests/integration/presentation-template.test.ts","tests/integration/scripts.test.ts","scripts/preview-process.mjs","scripts/verify.mjs","scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs","src/scripts/preview-process.test.ts"],"marker":"","scope_repair":[],"criterion":"engineering-tests-isolate-resources","cycle":"initial","part":0},{"id":"engineering-tests-wait-on-state","classification":"confirmed","rationale":"The criterion fails a browser test only when it waits a fixed time instead of waiting for state before asserting the step. It also fails one that treats a call returning immediately as if it waited. The two integration suites are quoted in full and contain no sleeps. Their only setTimeout calls kill a child process that runs too long (scripts.test.ts:25, presentation-template.test.ts:20). The only other timed wait is the 1000 ms socket timeout in the connect probe (scripts.test.ts:170), which caps how long the probe can take. Each test awaits the child&#39;s exit before asserting on its exit code and output. The browser scripts these tests run gate every step check on a state wait. In verify.mjs, line 71 waits for the presentation root before the first read at line 78. For each later step, line 100 polls with waitForFunction until data-step-index equals the next index, so the read at line 78 never stands in for a wait. The title and caption reads at lines 87 and 93 come after a mode-attribute waitForFunction (lines 84 and 90) and a visibility wait (lines 86 and 92). In inspect-presentation.mjs, each step waits on data-step-index at line 57 before anything else. Its waitForTimeout(settle) at line 59 comes after that state wait has confirmed the step. The timeout clause is met: there is a 30 s timer in startPreview. The build-first clause is also met: both scripts await `npm run build` before startPreview. The parsing clause is not met. Readiness depends on the server&#39;s printed `Local:` URL, and the review guidance names output split across chunks as a failure case. In both copies of preview-process.mjs, the ANSI strip `chunk.replace(/\\u001b\\[[0-9;]*m/g, &#39;&#39;)` runs on each chunk before it is appended. If a colour escape is split between two chunks, neither half matches, and the stray bytes stay in `output`. The URL regex `/Local:\\s+(http:\\/\\/127\\.0\\.0\\.1:\\d+\\/?)/` also has no terminator after the port digits. A chunk that ends mid-port, such as `...127.0.0.1:41` followed by `73/`, matches at once and resolves `settled` with a truncated, wrong URL. The readiness parsing therefore does not tolerate output split across chunks. Judge A&#39;s pass rests on the claim that matching accumulated output handles split chunks. The source contradicts that claim in both cases above. preview-process.test.ts writes each Local line as one clean, uncoloured chunk, so no test covers either case.","citations":["scripts/preview-process.mjs","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/preview-process.mjs","src/scripts/preview-process.test.ts"],"evidence":["scripts/preview-process.mjs:25 output += chunk.replace(/\\u001b\\[[0-9;]*m/g, &#39;&#39;) strips ANSI codes per chunk, so an escape split across chunks survives in the accumulated output.","scripts/preview-process.mjs:26-29 match /Local:\\s+(http:\\/\\/127\\.0\\.0\\.1:\\d+\\/?)/ has no end anchor after the digits, so a chunk ending mid-port resolves readiness at once with a truncated port.","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/preview-process.mjs:25-29 has the same code; both verify and inspect copies depend on it.","src/scripts/preview-process.test.ts:36 writes the full uncoloured line &#39; Local: http://127.0.0.1:43127/\\n&#39; in one chunk; there is no split or ANSI case.","The other two clauses hold (preview-process.mjs:34 has the 30 s timeout; verify.mjs:41 and inspect-presentation.mjs:36-40 await the build), but the criterion fails when any one clause is unmet.","quoted lines: scripts/preview-process.mjs:22-36","quoted lines: skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/preview-process.mjs:22-36","quoted lines: src/scripts/preview-process.test.ts:30-38","decider ruling: fail, confirmed by the closed-world span audit"]}},{"id":"engineering-tests-wait-on-state","vote":"pass","result":{"id":"engineering-tests-wait-on-state","verdict":"pass","rationale":"The tests that drive a browser are the two integration suites, tests/integration/scripts.test.ts and tests/integration/presentation-template.test.ts. Neither has a sleep: the only setTimeout in either, at scripts.test.ts:25 and presentation-template.test.ts:20, is a kill-on-timeout guard. Each test awaits the child&#39;s &#39;exit&#39; event and then asserts on the exit code and output. The only other bounded wait is the socket timeout at scripts.test.ts:170, a connect probe that settles when the probe resolves. In the browser scripts, every step assertion is preceded by an auto-waiting or polling wait on state. verify.mjs waits for the presentation root locator at line 71 (timeout 10000) and again for visibility at line 77. It waits for the mode attribute with waitForFunction at lines 84 and 90, for the title and caption locators to be visible at lines 86 and 92, and for data-step-index to equal the next step with waitForFunction at line 100. So the getAttribute read at line 78 always follows a state wait: line 71 for the first step, and line 100 from the previous iteration for later steps. It is not an immediate read used as a wait. inspect-presentation.mjs likewise waits for the root at line 49 and polls data-step-index with waitForFunction at line 57 before each later step. The jsdom component tests also use polling waitFor on data-step-index (Presentation.test.tsx:42-46, how-to-make-a-presentation.test.tsx:45). Judges A and B voted pass, and that is the ruling. Judge C points to inspect&#39;s `await page.waitForTimeout(settle)` (inspect-presentation.mjs:59) and the test&#39;s elapsed-time check `toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(300)` (scripts.test.ts:140). That fact does not decide the requirement. The criterion fails a test only when it sleeps a fixed time instead of waiting for state before asserting the step. Here the settle delay runs only after the state wait for the step index at line 57 has already confirmed the step. It is an extra animation settle before the screenshot, not a stand-in for the step wait. The elapsed-time assertion only checks that the --settle option is honoured. It is a time check, not a sleep in the test. dispute_checks{"demo-integration":[],"scene-kit":[],"presentation-skill":[],"verification-tooling":[],"engineering-quality":[{"id":"engineering-preview-readiness-bounded","classification":"confirmed","rationale":"The material shows what the auditor says. In both copies of preview-process.mjs, the ANSI strip runs on each chunk before it is appended to `output`, and the Local-URL regex runs on the accumulated text. If a colour escape sequence is split across two chunks, neither half matches /\\u001b\\[[0-9;]*m/. The stray escape bytes stay in the accumulated text, between `Local:` and `http://` or inside the URL. The match then fails, and readiness waits until the 30 s timeout. The criterion requires parsing that tolerates both ANSI codes and output split across chunks. Its guidance names this failure: matching that breaks on colour codes or split output, &#39;such as a per-chunk regular expression over raw coloured output.&#39; Because the guidance names the scenario, it is not a hypothetical outside the contract. The other two clauses hold, but the criterion fails when any one is unmet. The repository and template verify and inspect scripts both depend on this startPreview, so the defect reaches every delivered copy. The auditor&#39;s remark that the primary verdict &#39;concedes&#39; the gap is inaccurate, but that remark does not decide the outcome.","evidence":["scripts/preview-process.mjs and skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/preview-process.mjs: `output += chunk.replace(/\\u001b\\[[0-9;]*m/g, &#39;&#39;)` strips each chunk on its own, then `out…","Readiness depends on the printed Local URL: the promise resolves only from that match, and otherwise it rejects after 30 s.","Review guidance: fail when readiness depends on the printed ready URL and the matching breaks on ANSI colour codes or on output split across chunks, &#39;such as a per-chunk regular expression over r…","src/scripts/preview-process.test.ts writes only uncoloured lines (` Local: http://127.0.0.1:43127/`), with no ANSI case and no split-escape case.","The timeout clause and the build-before-preview clause hold: there is a 30 s readiness timeout, and both scripts await `npm run build` before calling startPreview."],"citations":["scripts/preview-process.mjs","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/preview-process.mjs","scripts/verify.mjs","scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/verify.mjs","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs","src/scripts/preview-process.test.ts"],"marker":"","stage":"contradiction-check","panel_index":0,"sample":1}],"testing-evidence":[],"assumption-handling":[]}
